question: Why did US unemployment rise in 2009?
summary: US unemployment rose in 2009: 7.3% (2008-12) -> 10.0% (2009-10 peak), +2.7 pts; 2007 average 4.6%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) construction employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak; (2) manufacturing employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak; (3) total payroll employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak.
supported: Total payroll employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
Construction employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
Manufacturing employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
Industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak

H1: Initial jobless claims rose during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H2: Total payroll employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H3: Leisure & hospitality employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H4: Construction employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H5: Manufacturing employment fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H6: Industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H7: The federal funds rate rose during the run-up to the 2009 peak

reference: Unemployment reached 10.0% in October 2009 in the recession; job losses were concentrated in construction and manufacturing (BLS Monthly Labor Review, 'Job losses in 2009', 2010).
